target_customer: Patients and caregivers living with ALS, Alzheimer's and related dementias, Parkinson's and Huntington's, paid through insurers, health systems and payers
problem: Neurodegenerative patients face scarce specialists and fragmented care; the company offers virtual specialist care with a coordinator.
business_model: virtual clinic billed to insurance and payer contracts, plus partnerships with health systems
product_category: virtual neurology care for neurodegenerative disease

founders.name: Peter Wallach
founders.role: Founding CEO and founder (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a recovering Bain consultant. A CityBiz listing (not opened) calls him CFO, co-founder and board member.

founders.name: Brian Wallach
prior_employers: Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher and Flom (associate)
US Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois (assistant US attorney 2014 to 2018)
Obama White House (senior vetting counsel 2011 to 2013)
founders.background_notes: Attorney and ALS patient, per the YC page.

founders.name: Martina de Majo
founders.role: Founder and Director of Research and Development
education: BS and MS in pharmaceutical biotechnology, University of Rome La Sapienza
PhD in clinical neuroscience, King's College London
founders.background_notes: Focused on iPSC derived in vitro models of neurodegenerative disorders, per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A telehealth practice built on video visits, scheduling and care coordination; the difficulty is clinical staffing, licensing in many states and payer contracting, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Multi state licensing, payer contracts and partnerships such as the ALS Association give some barriers, but virtual neurology practices can be copied by other clinics.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying it; later coverage names Harmonic Health and Isaac Health as other dementia and neurology care providers.

market_need_then: The company says patients leave clinics with paper referrals and no coordination. Brian Wallach's own ALS diagnosis in 2017 and his I AM ALS advocacy motivated the care model, per the company's story page.

identity.visual_style: Clean, teal and white palette with simple line icons per condition
identity.voice_and_tone: Reassuring and plain spoken; Expert Neurology Care, Made Simple

branding.community_and_virality: Partnership with the ALS Association announced April 2024 and press coverage of its Series A; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Association with I AM ALS and the ALS Association and trade press coverage give credibility, but the name is a hard to spell coinage and no source credits it for growth.

outcome_analysis: Synapticure combined an ALS patient advocate founder with a virtual specialist clinic, raised a seed round from GV and a 25 million dollar Series A led by B Capital in November 2024 with CVS Health Ventures and CommonSpirit Health, and later launched an ataxia program in July 2026. It is active and growing with payer and health system partnerships, with no layoffs or exit found.
notes: Founder and founding date conflict: several secondary outlets say the company was founded in 2022 by Sandra Abrevaya and Brian Wallach and list Abrevaya as CEO, while the YC page lists Peter Wallach, Brian Wallach and Martina de Majo and says 2019. The company story page could not be opened, so Abrevaya is not listed as a founder here. The seed round date is unknown; the 6 million dollar GV seed comes from a CityBiz headline and a search summary. CB Insights dates the Series A to September 24, 2024 versus November 2024 in press. Another source cites 31 million dollars publicly announced total; raising.fi says 10 million dollars plus, unverified. The 2024 Series A and the ALS Association partnership are after the 2020 batch. No competitor with a source dated near 2020 was found, so the list is empty.
